note: V6 sweep ledger — one v6 take and one v6-wild take per entry, fresh lyrics each. Clip ids collected at generation time (v6 rewrites metadata.tags, so opening-matching cannot recover them). Attach one clip per generation (batch_index v0).

v6-wild.title: Come On Back To The Water
The Last Light Before The Line

v6.title: Down Where The Water Is Wide

v6-wild.title: The Long Way Up The Hill
The Story I Tell About You

v6.title: The Light That Hunts The North
The Lights Came Up In Colour
Meet Me Where The Light Goes

v6-wild.title: The Last Train Is Not Coming

v6.title: The Slow Way Down The Coast
Takin' It Apart
v6.idea: someone taking apart, one piece at a time, the life they assembled with a person who is not coming back — and finding the last piece is a door they could have walked through years ago

v6-wild.title: Everybody Else Is Finished
v6-wild.idea: the long after of a death, when everyone else's mourning has a schedule and yours does not, and one hour of the day becomes the only thing that agrees with you

v6.title: Somebody's Gotta Keep It On
v6.idea: a person keeping something alive that nobody needs any more, because they are afraid of who they will be the day they stop reaching for it

v6-wild.title: The Way You Walk Ain't Yours
v6-wild.idea: following a stranger through a crowd because they move like someone you lost, and wanting the mistake to last as long as possible

v6.title: The Kindest Lie In Town
v6.idea: a kindness told so often and so well that it became the room two people live in, and neither will be the one to open the window

v6-wild.title: Still Ringing
v6-wild.idea: the state of being between two lives, and choosing to burn the one that can still be heard ringing

v6.title: Still Tuned In
v6.idea: someone who took the safe option once and has walked the same circuit ever since, still tuned to a station that stopped broadcasting

v6-wild.title: I'll Say It At The Gate
v6-wild.idea: admitting a thing at the last possible moment, in a place built for leaving, and finding the admission was written over an older one

v6.title: The Kind Thing
v6.idea: forgiving someone by never telling them what you know, and watching the not-telling quietly wear you both down

v6-wild.title: The Boxes Remember
v6-wild.idea: packing for a move made so many times the boxes remember it, and accepting that each leaving takes a smaller piece than the last

v6.title: What I Keep Under
v6.idea: the part of yourself kept submerged because it does not fit the life you built, and the way it surfaces at night

v6-wild.title: Glad For You
v6-wild.idea: watching someone get the thing you wanted, being glad for them out loud and meaning it, and carrying the shape of it behind your eyes all week

v6.title: Neither Won Nor Lost
v6.idea: a person who stopped chasing and cannot tell whether it is peace or surrender, and has decided not to find out

v6-wild.title: The Roof Is Only A Roof
v6-wild.idea: going back to the place where you were certain something terrible would happen, and finding the fear written over by ordinary years

v6.title: I Waved
v6.idea: greeting someone you wronged as though nothing happened, and both of you silently agreeing to the performance

v6-wild.title: I Like The Pull
v6-wild.idea: the pull toward a thing that will cost everything, and the honest admission that the pull is the part you love

v6.title: Never Did Happen
v6.idea: missing a version of your life that never actually happened, and the slow coming-apart of the story you told to keep it

v6-wild.title: Done Waitin'
v6-wild.idea: the night you finally stopped waiting for someone, and how unfairly beautiful the world was about it

v6.title: Good Morning
v6.idea: an old man walking the same morning loop past the spot where he nearly went over at twenty, and saying good morning to it

v6-wild.title: The Summer Everybody Left
v6-wild.idea: two kids burning a mattress in a rail yard the summer everyone else left town, and one of them still there at forty

v6.title: Nine Of 'Em Work
v6.idea: whoever runs the failing arcade telling a stranger exactly how bad the books are, and refusing to be pitied for it

v6-wild.title: Water On Tuesday
v6-wild.idea: still watering a plant that belonged to someone who left, with the shed radio tuned to the station the two of them used to argue about

v6.title: Neither Of Us Turns
v6.idea: a goodbye on a platform that has gone on too long, both people wanting it over, neither willing to be the one who turns first

v6-wild.title: Row Six On Sunday
v6-wild.idea: a man still pruning trees for an estate that has already been sold, walking the rows the day before the machines arrive

v6.title: Same Speed As You
v6.idea: walking behind a stranger on a coast path in fog, matching their pace because overtaking would feel rude, neither of you speaking

v6-wild.title: They've Done It Lovely
v6-wild.idea: being shown politely around your old house by the people who bought it and painted over everything

v6.title: Early
v6.idea: the one who is early for everything, standing in the warm tunnel air, arriving somewhere and already wanting the next thing

v6-wild.title: Under The Bar
v6-wild.idea: a kid too small for the ride, waiting by the rail and working out how the mechanism does what it does

v6.title: I'm Doing Fine
v6.idea: telling a dying relative from a phone box in the rain that everything turned out fine, when it did not

v6-wild.title: Light
v6-wild.idea: driving onto a boat with everything you own and feeling nothing but lightness, which is frightening

v6.title: Up There
v6.idea: a crane driver up in the cab at first light, above the gulls, listening to the whole port talk to itself on the radio

v6-wild.title: I Did Not Turn Round
v6-wild.idea: hearing your grandmother tongue spoken behind you on a platform in a city where nobody speaks it, and not turning round

v6.title: Trees Close Over
v6.idea: teaching a kid to drive at dusk down a lane where the trees close over, and the kid going quiet because it is beautiful

v6-wild.title: I Stopped Looking
v6-wild.idea: looking for one face in every crowd for years after they died, and the ordinary morning it stops happening

v6.title: Both Hands
v6.idea: the brother who let go of the pram handle for a second on a hill, and what it did to the way he holds things now

v6-wild.title: I Couldn't See Her Face
v6-wild.idea: the night you notice you have forgotten the face of someone you swore you never would, and are glad

v6.title: Boots Outside The Door
v6.idea: a long-haul driver who calls home every night and cannot say he wants to come back; the yodel is what he does instead of saying it, and a stranger in the next room tells him to go home

v6.title: We Reap The Frost We Sow
A Lifetime In A Single Day
Who Needs A Place To Land

method.from_45: Seeds dealt blind by tools/seed_deal.mjs before the entry style is read; idea committed from the seeds alone. Seeds are material the song passes through, never its subject. The genre summary governs only the scaffold meter/rhyme. Re-rolls allowed for absurdity only, never for genre fit, and logged.
method.from_64: Lyrics written by Gemini-3.6-Flash via toolbaz.com/writer/ai-writing-assistant. I fill only the [3 word Genre summary] slot; Gemini populates the adverb and the 3-word idea itself. Output is cleaned before Suno: drop the meta header line, bracket production directions (parens mean SUNG per the notation rule), split "(Direction: words)" into [Direction] + (words), and bracket bare section labels. Counter on the site reads Activity History n/10 per window.
